title: Security of the Equal-Key Two-Permutation Cipher
summary: No attack below two-to-the-n computational complexity was known for the equal-key construction with distinct permutations; whether it achieves that target security remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Assess $E_{k,k,k}(x)=Q(P(x\oplus k)\oplus k)\oplus k$ for $P\ne Q$ and target security $2^n$.

scope.domain: Cryptanalysis of an equal-key, two-permutation key-alternating block cipher.
parameters: k: the key reused at all three key-addition points
x: the input to the encryption map
P and Q: the two public permutations
n: the size parameter governing the target computational security
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the construction achieves computational security at the two-to-the-n target.

citations.label: Key-Alternating Ciphers in a Provable Setting: Encryption Using a Small Number of Public Permutations - (Extended Abstract)

progress.summary: The source singles out the case with all three keys equal and distinct public permutations, reporting no known attack below two-to-the-n computational complexity. Whether the construction attains that security target remains unresolved.
citation_labels: Andrey Bogdanov et al., Key-Alternating Ciphers in a Provable Setting: Encryption Using a Small Number of Public Permutations - (Extended Abstract)
